pages.title: Post-quantum signatures, priced
pages.summary: What ML-DSA-44 and the hash-based alternatives actually cost on the one signature this site controls, and why the crawler now sends two.
pages.navHint: what a PQ signature costs in bytes and milliseconds

pages.title: Octane, priced against no framework
pages.summary: Nextane's 60.9% win over Next.js, re-measured on the live demo, then given the row every framework benchmark leaves out: a site that ships no framework at all.
pages.navHint: what a framework's floor costs against no framework

pages.title: What a crawler name is worth
pages.summary: Sixteen identities against eleven sites: two invented user-agent strings cleared a wall four documented crawler tokens could not, one site caught the lie, and Reddit served a link-preview bot 1,640 words where a browser got one.
pages.navHint: what a crawler name is worth when nothing verifies it

pages.title: The config that types itself
pages.summary: Wrangler's hidden TypeScript config, converted on a real Worker: the upload came out byte-identical, a plain-text variable arrived in the type as its own value, and the Durable Object type went backwards.
pages.navHint: what a config that is a program buys, and what it loses

pages.title: Flags the docs don't list
pages.summary: Nineteen hidden flags in one CLI, and the control that separates an option being accepted from an option doing anything: a closed schema answers the first question for an exit code, and four cases here show what the second one costs when nobody asks it.
pages.navHint: how to tell an ignored option from an honoured one

pages.title: Pixels Instagram has no reason to resample
pages.summary: A converter that owns the 40 megapixel downscale so the platform arrives with nothing to do, and an MCP mode that lets a model run it against photographs that stay on your machine.
pages.navHint: hand Instagram pixels it has no reason to resample

pages.title: Half the light
pages.summary: A one pixel checkerboard reduces to sRGB 188 and every resizer says 128, the browser's canvas included. The kernels already agree to seven decimal places, so what is left is the colour space, plus the five other defects that survived measurement because the instrument agreed with them.
pages.navHint: a checkerboard, and six instruments that could not see the defect

pages.title: Break-even at three submits
pages.summary: htmx 4.0 costs 11.46 KiB Brotli and saves 3,968 bytes per form submit, measured on the one page here whose shape it was built for. Break-even is 2.96 submits per visitor and the form is submitted once.
pages.navHint: what a hypermedia library costs a site with nothing to swap
